uh ok so one thing about this for the @GUIDING_LIGHT.md  and this was a thing i fought with claude about before with the whole rle pixel storage and dithering and i have the solution and it beats storing the png by miles. and extends to letting us also use animated shaders so uh let me try and articulate this best i can.

we want to store the layers with colors, but we want to also store the brush strokes. here is why and what i believe it looks like in practice:
we want to score as much memory as we possibly can. the best way to do this is by storing the color as a reference for the texture, but we also need to make sure we get the full texture of colors, and rle eats shit from dithering because of exactly what dithering does. and we have a 'dithering' paint brush which i love to use. so we store the brush strokes, we store the dithering variables that are in the strokes and we treat this as a function ready to accept that payload of strokes and density and whatnot of the dithering to apply to the texture, and then it runs once at runtime and is then loaded in with the most possible memory saved. this extends perfectly to animations because animations just become another payload of frame timings to the paint encodings for the engine to evaluate once on load and then its baked in
resolution: Captured the user's paint-storage ruling into GUIDING_LIGHT.md ('Worked Example: painted textures') and memory. The ruling: store painted textures as the paint PROGRAM — strokes carrying colour/shader-ink references plus the brush recipe including the dither variables (density/pattern/seed) plus the stroke path — replayed ONCE at load into the resident texture, never the rasterized RGBA (no PNG, no RLE of pixels). Rationale is the One Law on the image axis: dithering is high-frequency by design so its rasterization is the worst case for RLE and bloats PNG, but the scatter is generated by a few numbers, so store the numbers (formula) not the scatter (product); it is the bake lever pointed at load not disk (Discipline 2, CPU produces the artifact once at load). Animation extends it as the same program plus a frame-timings payload, baked once on load. This resolves the prior RLE-dead-end and PNG-blob-bloat fights. This req is the DOCTRINE capture only; the record-strokes→replay-at-load IMPLEMENTATION is a proposed follow-on vertical (a paint-program format, stroke capture in the model-paint path, and a Zig replay-at-load pass) awaiting the user's go.
